bib.title: HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units
bib.venue: IEEE ACM Trans. Audio Speech Lang. Process. 2021

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "HuBERT: Self-Supervised Speech Representation Learning by Masked Prediction of Hidden Units", by Hsu, Bolte, Tsai, Lakhotia, Salakhutdinov and Mohamed. The PDF is arXiv:2106.07447v1 (14 Jun 2021), a preprint. It does not carry the IEEE/ACM TASLP venue, so the course should cite it as TASLP 2021 only if you confirm that from somewhere else.

COVERAGE: I read all 52,633 characters across all 10 pages, which is the full body plus Tables I–VII and the conclusion. The paper has no appendix. I skimmed the references for origins only.

CLAIMS
- claim: The hidden units are made by k-means clustering. Iteration 1 clusters MFCC features. Later iterations cluster the intermediate transformer-layer features of the previous HuBERT model.
  number: 100 clusters on MFCC, then 500 clusters
  setup: k-means on 39-dim MFCC (13 coefficients plus first- and second-order derivatives) over LibriSpeech 960h. Later iterations fit on a 10% sample using scikit-learn MiniBatchKMeans (mini-batch of 10,000 frames, k-means++ with 20 starts).
  quote: "we run k-means clustering with 100 clusters on 39-dimensional MFCC features" / "we run k-means clustering with 500 clusters on the latent features extracted from the HuBERT model pre-trained in the previous iteration (not fine-tuned) at some intermediate transformer layer"
  where: p.4
- claim: The schedule runs through three generations. BASE iteration 1 trains on MFCC labels. BASE iteration 2 trains on labels from layer 6 of iteration 1. LARGE and X-LARGE train once on labels from layer 9 of BASE iteration 2, so they count as third-iteration models.
  number: 250k + 400k steps (BASE, 32 GPUs); 400k steps (LARGE on 128 GPUs, X-LARGE on 256 GPUs)
  setup: BASE pretrains on LibriSpeech 960h. LARGE and X-LARGE pretrain on Libri-Light 60,000h.
  quote: "we extract features from the 9-th transformer layer of the second iteration BASE HuBERT for clustering ... these two models can also be seen as the third iteration models."
  where: p.4
- claim: The loss is computed on masked frames only (α=1). This choice is what makes the method tolerate poor targets: with MFCC k-means units, putting the loss on unmasked frames causes training to fail.
  number: 17.86 vs 29.57 vs 96.37 dev-other WER (C=100, α=1.0/0.5/0.0)
  setup: Ablation pretrained for 100k steps and fine-tuned on 10h, reporting dev-other with an n-gram LM. Masking selects p=8% of frames as span starts with span length l=10, following SpanBERT and wav2vec 2.0.
  quote: "mask span is set to l = 10, and p = 8% of the waveform encoder output frames are randomly selected as mask start"; Table V row "100 0.243 17.86 29.57 96.37"
  where: p.4, p.8
- claim: Clustering on learned features gives far better units than clustering on MFCC, measured by phone-normalized mutual information (PNMI), the share of phone-label uncertainty that the cluster label removes. Better units give lower WER.
  number: PNMI 0.276 to 0.637 to 0.704; WER 18.40 to 11.91 to 10.75 (C=500)
  setup: Same ablation setup as the previous claim (Table V).
  quote: "K-means on BASE-it1-layer6 500 0.637 11.91" / "K-means on BASE-it2-layer9 500 0.704 10.75"
  where: p.8
- claim: There are three model sizes, all at a 20 ms frame rate (320x downsampling of 16 kHz audio). The text calls them 90M, 300M and 1B parameters, while Table I lists the exact counts.
  number: 95M / 317M / 964M
  setup: Architecture follows wav2vec 2.0, with 12, 24 and 48 transformer layers.
  quote: "Num. of Params 95M 317M 964M"
  where: p.3
- claim: HuBERT matches or beats wav2vec 2.0 on every fine-tuning split, with two exceptions at 100h, each 0.1 WER worse. The test-other figures below are HuBERT LARGE (Transformer LM) vs wav2vec 2.0 LARGE, both pretrained on Libri-Light 60k, with X-LARGE in brackets.
  number: 10min 7.6 vs 8.2 [6.8]; 1h 5.4 vs 5.8 [4.8]; 10h 4.6 vs 4.9 [4.0]; 100h 3.9 vs 4.0 [3.5]; 960h 3.3 vs 3.3 [2.9]
  setup: CTC fine-tuning with the CNN encoder frozen, decoded with a Transformer LM.
  quote: "the HuBERT LARGE model can achieve a WER of 4.7% on the test-clean set and 7.6% on the test-other set, which is 0.1% and 0.6% WER lower, respectively than the state-of-the-art wav2vec 2.0 LARGE model"; Table III "HUBERT X-LARGE LL-60k Transformer 1.5 2.5 1.8 2.9"
  where: p.5–7

LIMITS:
- At 960h, HuBERT only ties the best pretraining results (Table III, p.6). It "lags behind methods combining pre-training with self-training" (2.9 test-other vs 2.6 for Conformer XXL + Noisy Student). The claim that it would close the gap with self-training is a hope the paper does not test.
- Training takes multiple phases, which the authors concede when they "plan to improve the HuBERT training procedure to consist of a single phase."
- The only downstream task is English read-audiobook ASR (LibriSpeech and Libri-Light). The paper does not evaluate other languages, noisy or conversational speech, or speaker and emotion tasks.
- It also does not use the units for generation or as tokens for a speech LM. That is listed as future work only ("downstream recognition and generation tasks beyond ASR"). This matters for your "audio as tokens" section: the paper does not show that the units work as generation tokens.
- k-means on high-dimensional features does not fit in memory, so it is fit on a 10% sample. Ablations run at 100k steps with fixed hyperparameters.

BUILDS ON:
- DeepCluster [23]. Its reference entry did not extract cleanly, so I give no year.
- wav2vec 2.0 (Baevski et al., arXiv 2006.11477, 2020), the architecture and baseline.
- DiscreteBERT (Baevski, Auli, Mohamed, arXiv 1911.03912, 2019), the closest prior work.
- vq-wav2vec (Baevski et al., 2019).
- SpanBERT (Joshi et al., TACL 2020), the masking scheme.
- BERT (Devlin et al., 2018).
- Iterative pseudo-labeling (Xu et al., 2020).
- k-means (Lloyd, IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory, 1982).
- LibriSpeech (Panayotov et al., ICASSP 2015) and Libri-Light (Kahn et al., ICASSP 2020).

FIGURES:
- Fig. 1, p.2: "The HuBERT approach predicts hidden cluster assignments of the masked frames (y2, y3, y4 in the figure) generated by one or more iterations of k-means clustering." It is the best candidate: one picture shows that the targets are offline k-means IDs and that the loss applies only under the mask, which helps contrast semantic units with codec tokens.
- Fig. 2, p.7: unit quality per layer. Iteration 1 peaks around layer 6 and its last layers degrade.

PROBLEMS:
- The PDF has no embedded instructions.
- Two-row cells in Table IV and Table VII extracted merged (e.g. "0.251± 0.001 0.253 ± 0.001 0.253 ± 0.001500 0.283…"), so I did not quote them.
- The DeepCluster reference [23] did not extract cleanly.
- I could not verify the TASLP venue from the PDF.
